title: Computer Graphics and Generative Models
weeklyTopics: Generative models applied to 3D content creation
workloadNotes: Five individual programming assignments (60% total, 12% each, including a Blender project), a final exam (25%), and participation (15%: lecture discussion, Piazza, lab attendance, with up to +3% discretionary). Late homework: 10% flat penalty for up to 10 days, then 25%. Undergrad (498) and grad (598) students share lectures and assignments but are graded within separate tracks. Collaboration is encouraged but code must be rewritten independently afterward (MOSS plagiarism detection used); generative AI tools are prohibited for code generation.
prerequisitesText: EECS 281, and (MATH 425 or 412 or EECS 301 or IOE 265 or TO 301), and (EECS 351 or MATH 214/217/296/417/419 or ROB 101), or graduate standing. Familiarity with deep learning and computer vision strongly recommended for the generative-modeling portion.
textbooks: Marschner & Shirley, Fundamentals of Computer Graphics, 4th ed. (recommended, not required)
